segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
36 and villages.
And they killed all the captives,
and cast fire among the corpses,
so that by means of the great smoke,
that which also darkened the sun,
they might be able to subdue the city.
And when they had besieged it for three days,
they heard that the Romans and the Arabs who were with Maurice had arrived;
and they left and departed toward Callinicum.
The Romans, however, overtook them,
and destroyed many of them.
Now Tiberius, in his fourth year, fell ill with a belly ache and wasting {OCR?} of the bowels.
And when he knew that he was dying,
he gave his daughter Augusta as wife to Maurice, who was from Arabissus in Cappadocia,
and placed upon him the royal crown.
And after two days he died.
Twenty years [of reign].
In the first year of his reign,
a son was born to him by Augusta, the daughter of Tiberius,
and he was named Theodosius, born in the purple (Porphyrogenitus).
And at that time the Romans rebelled against Maurice,
and set up {OCR?} Germanus as leader over themselves.
And when Hormizd, king of the Persians, heard [this],
he sent {OCR?} them promises that they should be with him.
They, however, spurned him,
and came against him for battle.
And they captured three thousand Persian slaves,
and sent [them] {OCR?} to Maurice.
And they obtained pardon,
and returned to the king's allegiance,
and were received with joy,
while the king bestowed gifts and honors upon Germanus.
And in his fourth year,
there stirred up and went forth from the East the repulsive people of the Avars with braided hair,
and from the West also the Slavs and the Lombards.
And they came under the subjection of the Khagan, king of the Khazars,
and captured two cities from the Romans and many fortresses.
And were it not for the great trench {OCR?} which the king made outside of Adrianople,
their faces were even set toward Constantinople.
The Romans, however, hired the people of the Antes {OCR?},
(of the Antae {OCR?}):
and they fell upon Sclavonia, subdued it, and plundered it.
Now when the Slavs heard this,
they wrought great devastation in the territory of the Romans and returned.
